title: Cyrus and the Orchard
premise: In the winter of 1893, widowed lighthouse keeper Bram Montrose tends her light on a storm-battered coast, convinced history belongs to other people—until a sealed letter washes ashore naming the Montrose family in an old smuggling conspiracy that cost a man his life decades ago. As magistrates and vengeful descendants close in, Bram learns her late husband helped hide the truth, and that the family's inheritance—and its guilt—now rests on her silence. When the conspirators' last living heir must flee on the morning tide, only one berth remains on the ship, and Bram must decide whether to give it to the son who lied to her or the daughter who told her the truth. She gives it to neither: she testifies instead, surrendering the family name to justice outside the law and keeping the lighthouse—and the truth—for herself.
about_author: Ines Yarrow is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing coastal shipping records before turning to fiction. She writes from a rented cottage near the sea, where she collects storm glass and old letters.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine winter of tending the light is established: her grief for husband Ewan, her estrangement from his siblings, and her creed that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet isolation mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. After a violent gale she finds a waterproof satchel on the rocks containing a sealed letter addressed to 'the Montrose keepers,' describing a cargo gone wrong in 1861 and a man left to drown. Emotional beat: dread displacing solitude.

chapters.title: A Family of Careful Silences
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram and brother-in-law Aldous Montrose. Bram confronts Aldous in town; he admits the letter is real but begs her to burn it, revealing Ewan knew. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Maren Kell, daughter of the drowned man, arrives posing as a supply buyer, hunting proof of who killed her father. She befriends Bram without revealing herself. Emotional beat: two lonely women circling the same wound.

chapters.title: Ewan's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Searching Ewan's effects, Bram finds his hidden ledger matching the letter's dates—he was paid to keep the light dark one night. Emotional beat: betrayal of the dead husband she idealized.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Patience
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. A magistrate with his own debts begins asking questions; Aldous tries to buy silence and implicates himself further. Emotional beat: fear curdling into self-preservation.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals her identity to Bram during a rising storm; together they decode the ledger and realize the surviving heir of the plot is preparing to flee by ship. Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared grief.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The conspirators offer Bram passage and money to disappear with them; refusing means ruin, accepting means complicity. The ship sails at morning tide with a single berth left. Emotional beat: the choice compressed to a single night.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Climax, Bram's POV. At dawn Bram lights the lamp, signals the harbor patrol, and names every guilty party—including Ewan—in open testimony as the ship leaves without its passenger. Emotional beat: grief and liberation at once.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Record
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, coda. Justice is uneven but real; the Montrose inheritance is seized, yet Bram keeps the lighthouse and gives Maren her father's recovered logbook. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, truth kept like a flame.
